body:
## Summary
The studio's step navigation has four writers (rail click, `[`/`]`, a `?step=` that changes, the initial open) and two stores of 'where am I' (component state and the address) that drift apart. Move every transition into one pure reducer, `studioNav.ts`, and make the address the mirror of the active step, so the 24 in-step hand-offs land every time and a reload returns to the step you chose.

## Description
Today the active step is `phaseKey` state, the URL keeps whatever `?step=` the studio was opened with, and three hand-written code paths try to reconcile them with `seenWanted` and `initialWanted` refs. Three defects follow, all on b08bc7e: (1) after any rail click the address still names the deep-linked step, so a reload opens the wrong step and contradicts the bookmark just parked; (2) a hand-off Link to the step the address already names (ScriptStep's 'Open Research' after arriving at ?step=research) changes no search param and is swallowed; (3) a hand-off back to the originally deep-linked step moves the rail but is refused a park by the `initialWanted` early return. The adjacency rule and the park-reread-report block are each written twice, and three `setProject` writers race without an ordering token.

The move: `studioNav.ts` exports `NavState {door, active, url, project, seq}`, `NavEvent` (opened, failed, railPicked, bracket, urlChanged, refreshed, lockResult) and `step(state, event) -> {state, effects}` with effects `park(key) | replaceUrl(key) | reread`. It is React-free and imports only lib/projects. StudioView becomes a runner: `useReducer` over `step`, one effect executor (park + reread + reportStorageTrouble once; `router.replace` with the other query params preserved and `scroll:false`), and the window key handler dispatching `bracket`. Stepper imports `neighbour`. `router.replace`, not push: this card changes no history semantics.

## Flow
- Write the 8 cases against the not-yet-existing `studioNav.ts`; watch them fail (module missing, then wrong effects).
- Build the reducer; port StudioView's open/pick/urlChanged/bracket/sign-off results onto dispatch; delete seenWanted/initialWanted/pickRef.
- Stepper.onKeyDown uses `neighbour`; keep `data-testid=step-<key>`, aria-current and preload untouched.
- Keep the door retry's `attempt` nonce and update studio-door-retry's source pin only if the deps move.
- Regenerate the kit census; run the full suite and build.

## Expected impact
Every in-step hand-off (24 producers) lands and parks; reload and copy-link name the step on screen; the bookmark and the address can no longer disagree. StudioView loses ~60 lines of reconciliation. WORKSPACE-A 2b's eventual 'progress changed' notification gets a single place to land (`refreshed` with seq) instead of a fourth setProject writer.

## Evaluation
Claim: studio navigation becomes one pure transition function and the three hand-off defects close.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (the module does not exist; cases 4-6 describe live defects)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - tests/golden-path/studio-nav.probe.spec.ts (Node probe lane, no DOM) plus step-sign-off, studio-door-retry, project-outputs probes unchanged, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run check:kit-census`
Result: better
Gate: architecture

body:
## Summary
The shelf already knows each project's next move and offers it as one press; the studio, where the work actually happens, does not. Put the same verb on the project's title line, derived from the same rule, so locking a step hands you to the next one and a blocked step elsewhere is one press away.

## Description
`nextAction` (shelf.ts:188) is the product's worst-news-first answer to 'where does this project need me'. The race sheet draws it ('Up next', RaceSheet.tsx:397-411). Once inside the studio the answer disappears: the rail shows marks but a blocked Score while you work on Script is a small triangle you must notice, and after 'Lock step' nothing moves - you scan six marks and choose. The move is a pure `studioNext(project, active)` in `nextMove.ts` that returns `nextAction(project)` unless it names the step you are standing on or is 'Delivered' (then null), and a `NextMove` chip beside 'Lock step' that draws the verb with the step's tone and an arrow glyph. Pressing it, or the next-move key, calls `pick(step)` - the same door as a rail click, so it parks the bookmark and closes Outputs. No auto-jump: the chip offers, the user moves. No prose: the chip is a verb and a step name (the law in CLAUDE.md), tone from the existing state classes so obsidian and almanac both read it, and the accessible name is the verb.

## Flow
- Write the 8 cases; watch the pure ones fail (module missing) and the ratchet fail (no chip).
- `nextMove.ts`: `studioNext` over `nextAction` - imports shelf.ts read-only, no second precedence.
- `NextMove.tsx`: one button, verb + ArrowRight, `data-testid="studio-next-move"`, hidden when null.
- StudioView: render it in the title-line control group; bind one key (not arrows, Space, J/K/L, [ ]) with the bracket handler's guards; add the row to STEP_KEYS.
- Census, full suite, build; photograph `studio-*` screens with cx-capture in both themes.

## Expected impact
Lock-then-advance goes from 'lock, scan six marks, click' to 'lock, press'. A blocked or awaiting-decision step anywhere in the project is named on the screen you are on, in the shelf's own words, so the shelf and the studio can never disagree about what is next.

## Evaluation
Claim: the studio offers the project's next move, derived from the shelf's rule, actionable in one press.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (module and chip absent; guards run against the new module)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - tests/golden-path/studio-next-move.probe.spec.ts (Node probe lane: pure studioNext over seedProjects + mkProject, plus a source ratchet), step-sign-off probe unchanged, typecheck, npm test, check:narration, check:kit-census, build
Result: better
Gate: direction
